item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
225
ABPZ20 KNHC 042324
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Sep 4 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located several hundred miles east of the Hawaiian Islands,
on Hurricane Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest
of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Marie, located several
hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure may develop well offshore of southwestern
Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible, and a
tropical depression could form around the middle of next week while
it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, remaining well offshore
of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...MARIE MAINTAINING ITS INTENSITY FOR NOW... As of 8:00 PM PDT Fri Sep 04 the center of Marie was located near 20.8, -119.0 with movement NW at 8 mph. The minimum central pressure was 967 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 100 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Marie Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026 
005 
WTPZ33 KNHC 050231
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026
 
...MARIE MAINTAINING ITS INTENSITY FOR NOW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.8N 119.0W
ABOUT 600 MI...965 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...967 MB...28.56 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located 
near latitude 20.8 North, longitude 119.0 West. Marie is moving 
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this general motion 
is expected to continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. A gradual weakening trend is expected to begin on Saturday 
and continue for the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 967 mb (28.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026 
196 
WTPZ43 KNHC 050232
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026
 
Marie continues to display a ragged eye surrounded by a large area 
of convection with cloud tops between -50 to -60C.  Some dry air 
still appears to be entraining into the core.  Recent subjective and 
objective satellite intensity estimates range from 75-94 kt.  Thus, 
the initial intensity will be held at 85 kt for this advisory.
 
Marie has turned toward the northwest, with an initial motion 
estimate of 305/7 kt.  Marie will continue moving slowly 
northwestward during the next few days as it passes in between a 
ridge to its west and ridging to its east.  By the middle of next 
week, an upper-level trough near the U.S. West Coast may cause what 
is left of Marie to turn more toward the north-northwest in 4 to 5 
days. The NHC track forecast is very similar to the previous 
forecast, and lies near the HFIP Corrected Consensus (HCCA) and the 
Google DeepMind (GDMI) ensemble mean. It should be noted that model 
spread is quite large beyond 2 to 3 days.

It appears as though Marie has already peaked in intensity (no more 
strengthening is expected).  Although vertical wind shear is 
expected to remain low for the next 3 days, Marie will be moving 
into gradually cooler water temperatures as well as a drier air 
mass.  By 48 hours, water temperatures will be below 26C and the 
mid-level relative humidity will be below 50 percent.  The NHC 
intensity forecast shows Marie weakening to a tropical storm by hour 
48, and it shows a slightly faster weakening compared to the 
previous forecast.  The intensity forecast is still near the higher 
end of the guidance suite.  Marie is likely to lose its convection 
by day 5 and become a post-tropical cyclone, and that scenario is 
indicated by both the GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite imagery.
